title: Identical verdicts on different items are suspect
statement: When one prompt asks a model to judge several items, treat identical verdicts on different items as a reason to re-check them.
example: A judge gave two different takes the same scores and the same gap at 0:29, though one had no pause of 0.9 s or more.
detail: A blind pass judged seven voice takes in one request. Two different takes got the same scores, the same 'audio gap or cut around 0:29' and the same one-line verdict, yet a silence measure found no gap of 0.9 s or more in one of them, and the decision record read the other's gap as an ordinary sentence pause. The evidence is one pair in one pass, so it is a reason to look again, not a measured rate.
against: Identical verdicts can be right: in the same pass the four takes that read the prompt aloud got identical scores and the same issue, and all four did read it (g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/judging/judgments.json, lines 50, 74, 86 and 110; g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/DECISION.md, line 37). The 0.9 s silence measure also cannot rule out a shorter pause or a cut at 0:29.
